newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela Casma field could produce 12,000 bpd.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela Casma field could produce 12,000 bpd.

text.p: Oil output at Venezuela's Casma- Anaco field, sold at auction Monday for $27.58 million to a domestic consortium, could grow to 12,000 barrels per day from current levels of around 1,500 bpd, a consortium spokesman said.

The consortium -- made up of operator Cosa-Ingenieros Consultores with a 20 percent holding, financing group Cartera de Inversiones Venezolanas CA with a 50 percent holding, and equipment supplier Phoenix International CA with 20 percent -- was among 13 bidders on the first day of Venezuela's third round of oil operating contract auctions.
Cartera de Inversiones president Victor Vargas said at least 60 percent of the group's financing would come from international banks.
"The world's third largest investment bank will supply 60 percent of the financing ... We've also have offers from U.S. banks," he told reporters.
"The possibility was there to invest our country, and we took it," he added, commenting on the consortium's successful bid
The field has 29 million barrels of proven reserves, according to estimates by Venezuelan state oil company PDVSA.

Under the 20-year contract, the operator will produce hydrocarbons on behalf of PDVSA subsidiary Corpoven in exchange for a fee worked out on a sliding scale. As a condition of the contract, the operator must invest at least $6 million within three years, although PDVSA expects investment to be higher.
